readout_other: Tri-axial accelerometer recordings of resting/postural tremor (wing-beating position in ET; foot-tapping-induced hand tremor in PD), analysed via power spectral density
direction_notes: TUS to the Vim produced statistically significant tremor reduction overall and in ET patients specifically; PD patients showed only a modest, non-significant change, consistent with an inhibitory neuromodulatory effect on the thalamus.
safety_notes: The procedure lasted approximately 2 hours and was well tolerated by the participants, with no reports of paresthesia or any adverse effect.

exposures.label: Multi-focus TUS to left/right Vim of thalamus (ET and PD patients)

target.label: ventral intermediate nucleus (Vim) of the thalamus

timing.protocol_description: Multi-focus phased-array TUS delivered via optically-tracked neuronavigation guided by acoustic simulation (Babel-Brain); multiple focal spots were used on and around the intended Vim target to increase the effective stimulation area and mitigate small targeting errors. The whole procedure lasted approximately 2 hours; tremor was measured with an accelerometer before and after TUS delivery.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Eighteen patients, 11 ET (9 male; median age: 72; range: 62–82) and 7 PD (6 male; median age: 64; ranging: 52–73) patients, participated in an open-label study (no sham control). Subject demographics, baseline clinical scores, treatment hemisphere and strategy used are shown in Table S1. Three participants (1 ET and 2 PD) were excluded from the analysis due to incomplete data collection. Five ET participants underwent contralateral MR-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy prior to TUS.

flags.reason: 18 patients were enrolled but 3 were excluded from analysis for incomplete data collection (n=15 analysed); enrolled number (18) is reported here per convention, flagged for the enrolled/analysed discrepancy.
the paper does not explicitly state the number of TUS sessions per participant; the procedure is described as a single ~2 hour session but this is not stated in session-count terms.
the phased-array transducer and driving hardware are not named/attributed to a manufacturer in the main text.
pulse duration is not explicitly stated in the main text; only PRF (100 Hz) and duty cycle (10%) are given, from which pulse duration could be computed (1 ms) but this was not done per instructions.

the abbreviation for the reported in-situ intensity is garbled in the source text ('I ' with a missing subscript); interpreted as spatial-peak pulse-average intensity (ISPPA) based on the wording 'spatial-peak pulse-average intensity'.
